subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2) — Elara Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Carter <jamie.carter@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode & compliance: HIPAA/BAA, SOC2 — post-call recap

Hi Jamie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for Elara Health's PHI workloads.

Key notes from the call:
- Primary data class: PHI (medical records + PII) for triage and summarization workflows.
- Required compliance controls: HIPAA coverage with signed BAA, SOC 2 Type II evidence for vendor controls, customer-managed KMS for key separation, and 7+ year audit log retention for specific lines of business.
- Scale: steady throughput with occasional peaks (expected 300-500 reqs/min).

Deployment options and our recommendation:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, but for PHI it requires a signed BAA plus strict contractual controls. Host-based multi-tenant offering limits some audit isolation; we typically recommend Hosted only for low-risk PHI patterns or where data is tokenized and not stored.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): supports BAA and stronger tenant isolation, can be configured with customer-managed KMS and longer log retention. Good middle ground for teams that want predictable throughput without full private ops.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended for high-risk PHI, strict audit requirements, or when Elara must control network boundary and HSM/KMS. Private supports full control over logging, retention, and on-prem key material.

Recommended path for Elara based on requirements: 1) Sign BAA, 2) review SOC2 Type II evidence, 3) pilot on Dedicated capacity (fastest PoC while meeting BAA/KMS needs), 4) evaluate Private if audit or legal requires customer-managed infrastructure or air-gapped environment.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attached our current SOC2 Type II report and our BAA template for your legal team to review (see attachments).
2) Can you confirm the strictest retention window and whether customer-managed KMS is required from day 1?
3) If yes to KMS/day-1, we'll provision a Dedicated trial with KMS integration and loop in engineering ops — timeline ~2 weeks.
4) Schedule a 45-min security call next week (Rishi will join) to go through controls and evidence.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf (PDF, 3.2MB); Redwood_BAA_Template_v2.docx (DOCX, 45KB); Redwood_Security_Checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 35KB)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the SOC2 report.

—
Marissa Cole

From: Jamie Carter <jamie.carter@elarahealth.com>

Cc: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@elarahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance: HIPAA/BAA, SOC2 — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few follow-ups from our security and compliance team: 

1) SOC2: do you provide a SOC2 Type II report with auditor name and period (we require the last 12 months of coverage)?
2) KMS: we require customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest and for tokenization keys — is that supported for Dedicated, or only on Private?
3) Audit logs: can you confirm granular audit logs (per-request with user and model version) and a configurable retention policy up to 7+ years?
4) BAA: will your standard BAA allow subprocessor disclosure and a clause for annual audits? Our legal wants to see redlineable copy.

Also: if we start on Dedicated for the PoC, will there be any feature differences vs Private (particularly around network egress controls and the ability to host within our VPC)?

Appreciate a clear callout of which requirements map to Hosted/Dedicated/Private so we can present to our CTO.

—
Jamie Carter
Senior Program Manager, Security & Compliance
Elara Health
jamie.carter@elarahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Carter <jamie.carter@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance: HIPAA/BAA, SOC2 — post-call recap

Jamie — great questions, answered inline below.

> 1) SOC2: do you provide a SOC2 Type II report with auditor name and period?
Yes — attached is our SOC2 Type II for the period 2024-09 through 2025-09, audited by NorthPoint Assurance. If you need a more recent attestation, we can provide a redacted bridge letter and work with our audit team for a disclosure timeline.

> 2) KMS: customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest and tokenization keys — supported for Dedicated or only Private?
We support customer-managed KMS for both Dedicated and Private. For Dedicated we integrate with your cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) and require an initial key exchange and IAM mapping. For Private on-prem we support bringing your HSM/KMS. Hosted API currently supports service-managed keys; we can discuss limited customer key workflows but they are not standard for Hosted in PHI scenarios.

> 3) Audit logs: granular per-request logs and retention up to 7+ years?
Yes — Dedicated and Private offer per-request audit logs (request id, user id, model version, timestamp, response hashes) and configurable retention policies. Hosted API provides standard logs but retention is limited by plan; we can export logs to your SIEM or long-term storage for Hosted in certain enterprise arrangements.

> 4) BAA: is your standard BAA redlineable and includes subprocessor disclosure and annual audits?
Our BAA template (attached) is intended to be redline-friendly. We disclose subprocessors and can provide a subprocessors list on request. We also include a clause for annual security attestations; if Elara requires additional audit rights we can escalate to our legal and security leadership to align contractually.

Feature differences: Dedicated vs Private
- Dedicated: tenant isolation, customer KMS integration, long log retention, predictable capacity; network egress is controlled via VPC peering or secure tunnels but the control plane remains Redwood-managed.
- Private: full control over network boundary (VPC/on-prem), optional air-gapped deployment, customer-managed control plane, and support for on-prem HSMs.

Proposed immediate steps:
- Please have legal review the attached BAA and send any redlines back to me.
- If you confirm customer-managed KMS and want a PoC, I will ask Rishi to open a Dedicated trial with KMS integration (estimate 10 business days to provision and test).
- Schedule a 45-min security deep-dive next Tue/Wed — Rishi (engineering ops) and Monica (solutions) will join.

DocuSign BAA: https://share.redwood.com/DocuSign/BAA_ELR_0421
SOC2 reference: https://redwood.app/docs/security/soc2

I can circulate a short mutual action plan once you confirm the timeline.

Thanks —
Marissa

Looping in on the ops side — we can provision a Dedicated trial with KMS integration scoped to Elara's account. Action items I will take: 
1) Open provisioning ticket and request required IAM roles & sample KMS key ARN from Elara.
2) Configure audit-log export to your S3 (or GCS/Azure) bucket for long-term retention; will provide template retention policy.
3) Stand up a test tenant and share runbook for validation (latency, model version pinning, KV cache behavior).

Estimated ETA: 8-10 business days once we have the KMS ARN and S3 export target. If Elara confirms they need air-gapped Private, we can draft a separate SOW and timeline (Private typically 6-8 weeks).
